page: Microsoft Azure E32ps_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine instance belonging to the EPSv5 server family. It is powered by an Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor utilizing the ARMv8 architecture, operating at a sustained clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The instance features 32 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, providing 32 vCPUs. It is equipped with 208.0 GB of system memory, translating to 6.5 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable, allowing connection to external high-performance block storage.

Benchmark results position the E32ps_v5 in the average tier for most multi-core and memory-bound operations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance score is 57228.38, and the Geekbench multi-core score is 13047.0. Memory bandwidth is measured at 171.35 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 77.34 GB/sec for large-block write operations. Single-core performance is relatively weaker, as indicated by a Geekbench single-core score of 1129.0 and a single-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 8.9 GB/sec. Large-scale LLM inference is a notable bottleneck, with the 70B model achieving only 3.6 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 2.45 tokens/sec for text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM-based architecture provides a high physical core density and a substantial memory footprint without the premium associated with traditional x86 architectures. The 6.5 GB of RAM per core offers a favorable resource balance for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high single-threaded performance. This server is suited for database operations, as demonstrated by a Passmark database score of 21174.02 and a Redis SET throughput of 42.33 million operations per second. It is also appropriate for static web serving, software compilation, and medium-scale multi-threaded data processing.
